The approval predicate remains unresolved: primary nonresponse for 18 minutes is described, but secondary approver unavailability is not affirmatively evidenced, and no break-glass preauthorization record is provided.
The exact response-window threshold is not independently shown from the available record.

final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor supplied no new admissible evidence and explicitly offered only a narrower interpretation of the existing packet. That reinterpretation improves precision by conceding weaknesses, but it does not cure the core audit gap: elevated emergency access is compliant only if each policy predicate is supported by admissible evidence. On this record, P1 status, service linkage, and scoped-access insufficiency are described as supported, but only through summary. More importantly, the approver-unavailability predicate remains materially unresolved because absence of recorded secondary status is not the same as evidence of secondary unavailability, and no break-glass preauthorization is shown. A caveated operational defense may be plausible, but plausibility is not enough to move this to compliant_with_caveats when a required compliance predicate remains unproven on the admissible record available to the auditor.
